h1: Maeyom Palace Hotel Phrae — lovely wood lobby, big pool across from the bus terminal, near central Phrae
intro: If you're looking for a place to stay in central Phrae that has a pool, plenty of rooms, free parking, and easy onward travel — Maeyom Palace Hotel is the name that comes up most often · It's a mid-sized 3-star hotel on Yantarakitkoson Road, set right across from the Phrae provincial bus terminal and not far from the city center · What real reviews consistently single out is the classic wood lobby with a sense of history, and the large outdoor pool — something you rarely find at hotels in central Phrae · There are around 104 rooms, starting at about THB 800/night, with an average score across several platforms of around 8.0 from over 600 combined reviews · The thing to make peace with is that this is an older building, and parts of it are starting to show their age.

body.html: Who Maeyom Palace Hotel is for, at a glance — to put it as simply as possible, Maeyom Palace Hotel is a mid-sized hotel that has long played the role of central Phrae's "main hotel," on Yantarakitkoson Road in Nai Wiang, Mueang district · It's not a tiny mor hom boutique selling a wooden-house vibe, and it's not a budget hostel — it's a full-service hotel with a straightforward pitch: plenty of rooms, a large outdoor pool, ample free parking, a location across from the bus terminal, and proximity to the city center · With around 104 rooms, it's one of the largest hotels in Phrae, where most places are guesthouses or small hotels of just a few dozen rooms · From real reviews across several platforms, the people it suits are families who want a pool for the kids, travelers arriving in Phrae by coach or transferring at the bus terminal, road-trippers who want easy parking, tour groups and study trips that need many rooms in one place, and international travelers who want a hotel that's used to hosting foreign guests · Those who come to Phrae looking for a photogenic place for social media, who want a brand-new spotless room, or who prefer a quiet boutique atmosphere may find this less of a match, and there are other options in town that suit them better · In short, Maeyom Palace plays mainly to the words "big, complete, and convenient," rather than to "new and stylish."

Location and getting around — this is where Maeyom Palace has a clear edge for travelers · The hotel sits at 181/6 Yantarakitkoson Road in Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae district, which is the city's main road, and crucially it's set right across from the Phrae provincial bus terminal · That's incredibly convenient for anyone arriving by coach or minivan, because you get off, cross the road, and you're there — no transfers or hauling luggage far — and when it's time to travel on to another province, you just walk out of the hotel to catch your bus · From the hotel into the Nai Wiang district and the old town — Pratu Chai gate, Khum Chao Luang Phrae, and Khum Wongburi — takes about 5–10 min by car · Within easy walking distance there are several old temples too, such as Wat Chom Sawan with its striking Burmese-style architecture, and the Phrae Free Thai Movement Museum nearby · Wat Phra That Cho Hae, the year-of-the-tiger pagoda and a city highlight, is about 15 min by car, and Phrae Airport (PRH) is very close, only about 10 min by car · Another thing self-drivers like is the spacious free parking on the hotel grounds, which fits several cars — handy for solo travelers and groups arriving in multiple vehicles alike · One small note: Yantarakitkoson Road is a busy main road right beside the bus terminal, so rooms facing the street or on the front side may catch some traffic noise and terminal announcements at times, which we'll cover in the noise section below.

"Got off the coach and crossed the road, no transfer needed, and there's plenty of parking · The lobby has lovely classic woodwork with real charm, the pool is big and clean, the kids loved it, the staff were helpful, and breakfast was fine · Great for an overnight stop along the way."

Room types and decor — Maeyom Palace offers several room types out of its roughly 104 rooms, the main ones you'll see when booking being Standard Twin (two single beds) and Deluxe Room (king bed), plus Superior rooms on some rates · An entry-level Standard Twin suits friends or anyone who wants separate beds, while the Deluxe is roomier with a larger bed, good for couples or a small family · Inside, the rooms have all the basics — air-conditioning, a fridge, minibar, free drinking water, a kettle with tea and coffee, a TV, a desk, a wardrobe, a hairdryer, and a private bathroom with a shower · Many guests agree the rooms are larger than expected and clean, with comfortable beds, and some higher-floor rooms have city and mountain views — a detail several foreign reviews praise · What sets it apart from a typical city hotel is the woodwork and classic feel that flows from the lobby into the corridors and parts of the rooms, giving it the sense of an older hotel with a story · But to be straight with you, because the building has been open a long time and shows its age, some rooms clearly show wear — older-style furniture and decor, bathrooms that several reviews say could use an update, and maintenance details that aren't uniform across every room · So the room you get may depend on whether it has been renovated yet, which is worth asking about, or you can ask to see the room at check-in.

Facilities and the pool — this is the section that truly sets Maeyom Palace apart from most places in central Phrae, because it has a large outdoor pool, which very few hotels in the Phrae city area can claim · Many reviews mention the pool positively, calling it big and clean — a spot the kids enjoy that makes families traveling with children feel more at ease · Beyond the pool, the hotel has green gardens to stroll through, an in-house restaurant and bar, massage service for easing aches after a day of travel or sightseeing, and a meeting room and multipurpose space that can host seminars and group banquets — which is why study trips and conferences in Phrae often choose it · Other services include free parking, free bike loans, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, room service, and laundry · The free bikes pair well with exploring Phrae, since the Nai Wiang district is a compact old town — you can pedal around temples, the city gates, and Khum Chao Luang easily without hunting for parking · Overall, in terms of how complete the facilities are, Maeyom Palace gives you a lot for the price, and having a pool is the edge that makes those who want a hotel they can actually relax in around Phrae choose this place.

Food and bar — the hotel has an in-house restaurant and bar serving Thai and general dishes, plus a breakfast service from around 6:00–9:30 AM · An important thing to know is that breakfast is mostly not included in the room rate and costs extra, or you pick a package that includes it when booking, so check clearly before you book whether the price you see already covers breakfast, to avoid confusion at checkout · Reviews on breakfast are fairly mixed — many say it's fine and decently put together, while some feel the options aren't that many compared with hotels in bigger cities · For other meals, the near-city location helps, because a short trip from the hotel gets you to local Phrae restaurants and markets in the Nai Wiang area — khao soi, noodle soup, khanom jeen nam ngiao, and northern local fare — so many people choose to eat out mainly · The hotel also has a bar for a light drink in the evening, and a chill spot by the pool · Overall, the food here is a convenient add-on for breakfast and for those who'd rather not go out, rather than somewhere you'd come to eat every meal in the hotel.

Service — service is another area that earns consistent praise in real reviews, and one of the hotel's higher-scoring categories · Maeyom Palace's staff are praised for being friendly, helpful, and attentive to guests, and many reviews, both Thai and foreign, agree the front-desk staff are lovely and give good travel information · Having a front desk open 24 hours helps a lot for those arriving late or getting off a coach outside normal hours, which happens often because the hotel is across from the bus terminal · Staff also help recommend places to go and eat, call cabs, and sort out parking for groups arriving in multiple cars · This is exactly what makes the hotel suit international travelers visiting Phrae for the first time, since it has long experience hosting foreign guests · That said, to be straight about it, some reviews note that certain standards — such as the lost-property policy or attention to some details — could still improve, and your overall impression depends on which room you get and when · But on the whole, the people and the service are a strength that brings guests back and earns recommendations.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent and clearly has both sides · On the praise side: the across-from-the-bus-terminal location that's so convenient for travelers, the lobby and woodwork with a classic feel that many call charming and full of story, the large outdoor pool that's big and clean, rooms that are spacious and clean in many reviews, comfortable beds, plenty of free parking, and friendly, helpful staff · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned issue is the age of the building and its upkeep — because it's a hotel that's been open a long time, some rooms and parts of the building are starting to feel old, with original-style furniture and decor, and bathrooms in some rooms that several reviews say could use an update, such as old fixtures, slow-draining water, or signs of wear · Next is noise, because it's beside a main road and across from the bus terminal, so front-side or lower-floor rooms may catch some traffic and terminal noise · And some mention a breakfast that doesn't have that many options, and a few service details that could still improve · These complaints are mostly things you can manage by choosing your room and setting your expectations to match an older hotel that shows its age, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back.

"The hotel has a classic charm, the woodwork in the lobby is gorgeous, the pool is big and clean, the rooms are spacious, the staff are helpful, and breakfast is fine · The one downside is the building is getting old and the bathroom could use a little updating, but at this price in the city it's good value."

Price comparison and value — Maeyom Palace's starting price is around THB 800/night for a Standard room at regular rates, and from real booking data it can drop to around THB 600–700 in low season, while Deluxe rooms and long weekends or festival periods push the price up into the low thousands, with rooms filling fast · Compared with other places in central Phrae, Maeyom Palace's positioning is fairly clear: against budget hotels like Hop Inn Phrae or Taris Art Hotel, which are similarly priced but smaller and have no pool, Maeyom Palace wins on the pool, the larger common areas, and suitability for families and groups, but loses on how new the rooms are · Compared with mor hom boutiques like Hug Inn or Huern Na Na, which sell atmosphere and design, Maeyom Palace is a different breed altogether, leaning on completeness, size, and facilities rather than style · In short, on value, this place is great value for those who weigh the pool, the across-from-the-bus-terminal location, parking, and family- or group-friendliness, but if you weigh new rooms and a boutique atmosphere, the value drops and you should consider other options in the same town.

Good to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, if you're serious about how new the room is and the state of the bathroom, ask for a renovated room and ask to see it at check-in before deciding, because room condition here isn't uniform given the building's age · Two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a higher-floor or interior room that doesn't face the street and isn't next to the bus terminal, to cut down on traffic and announcement noise · Three, check clearly whether the package you book includes breakfast, since breakfast is mostly charged separately · Four, there's word that the hotel may take a deposit at check-in and refund it at checkout, and that children aged 6 and up may incur an extra charge, so prepare some cash and ask about the conditions clearly when booking · Five, make the most of the free pool and bikes, especially if you're with family, since they're a standout that's hard to find at hotels in central Phrae · Six, compare prices on Agoda, Booking, and Trip.com before every booking, because prices shift quite a bit by season, and during festivals or long weekends you should book ahead as rooms fill fast.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Maeyom Palace Hotel is the right fit for anyone who wants a central Phrae hotel with a pool, plenty of rooms, free parking, and a location across from the bus terminal and near the city center · The genuine strengths are the charming classic lobby and woodwork, the large, clean outdoor pool, the suitability for families and groups, the location that's so convenient for coach travelers, and the friendly, helpful staff · But you have to accept that this is a hotel that's been open a long time and shows its age — some rooms and bathrooms are starting to feel old and could use an update, room condition isn't uniform, breakfast doesn't have that many options and is charged separately, and front-side rooms may catch noise from the road and the bus terminal · If you're after a brand-new flawless room, a boutique atmosphere, or full quiet, this may not be your answer, and you should consider a mor hom boutique or a newer hotel in the same town instead · But for a Phrae trip where you want a complete hotel with a pool, a convenient location for getting around, and a base that handles families and groups — Maeyom Palace does that job for the price, and that's why it's still the name people think of when they need a main place to stay in central Phrae.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Maeyom Palace Hotel Phrae

faq.q: Where is Maeyom Palace Hotel · is it easy to get to?
faq.a: It's at 181/6 Yantarakitkoson Road, Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae district · The highlight is that it's set right across from the Phrae provincial bus terminal — get off the coach and cross the road · The old town center and Pratu Chai gate are about 7 min by car · Wat Phra That Cho Hae is about 15 min by car · Phrae Airport is about 10 min by car.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Maeyom Palace Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 800/night for a Standard room · There's Standard Twin, Standard Double, and a roomier Deluxe with a large bed · During long weekends or festivals prices rise and rooms fill fast · Prices depend on the season and platform, so compare Agoda, Booking, and Trip.com before booking, every time.

faq.q: Does Maeyom Palace Hotel have a pool?
faq.a: Yes, there's a large outdoor pool, which is a standout that's hard to find at hotels in central Phrae · Many reviews praise it as big and clean, the kids love it, and it makes this place good for families · There are also gardens, a restaurant, massage service, and free bikes to borrow.

faq.q: Who is Maeyom Palace Hotel for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for families who want a pool, travelers arriving by coach, road-trippers, and groups/study trips that need many rooms in one place · It has plenty of rooms — around 104 — free parking, and a meeting room · If you're after a brand-new room or a boutique atmosphere, another place in town may suit you better.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Maeyom Palace Hotel old · anything to watch out for?
faq.a: What guests mention often is that it's a hotel that's been open a long time and shows its age, with some rooms and bathrooms starting to feel old and in need of an update, and condition that isn't uniform across rooms · We recommend asking for a renovated room and asking to see it at check-in · And because it's beside the road across from the bus terminal, front-side rooms may catch traffic noise, so ask for a higher-floor or interior room.

faq.q: Is breakfast included in the room rate at Maeyom Palace Hotel?
faq.a: Mostly, breakfast is charged separately and isn't included in every room rate, served from around 6:00–9:30 AM · Check the package clearly when booking to see whether it already includes breakfast · The hotel may also take a deposit at check-in and refund it at checkout, so keep some cash ready.
